title: Can't shift out of Park
h1: Why won't my car shift out of Park?
metaDesc: Shifter stuck in Park? See if it's the brake light switch, battery, shift lock or a hill, how to use the shift lock release, and when you need a tow.
synonyms: can't get car out of park
shifter won't move out of park
car won't come out of park
push button shifter stuck in park
brake pressed but shifter won't move
stuck in park no brake lights
intro: Automatic cars lock the shifter in Park until they sense your foot on the brake. When it won't move, the cause is usually small: a brake light switch, a blown fuse, a weak battery or the car's weight resting on the Park lock. A few questions will tell you which, and how to get moving safely.
safety: Set the parking brake before you try to force anything. If the shifter suddenly releases, the car could roll.
Don't drive without working brake lights. Drivers behind you won't know you're stopping.

q_what.q: What happens when you press the brake and try to shift out of Park?
q_what.help: Have the key in ON or the engine running, and press the brake pedal firmly before you try.

opts.a: The shifter is locked solid, or the button on the shifter won't press in
It feels jammed, and the car is parked on a slope
The shifter moves, but the dash still shows P or the car won't move
It's a push-button or dial shifter, and it won't change gears
The car is dead, or the dash lights are dim

q_brake_lights.q: Do the brake lights come on when you press the pedal?
q_brake_lights.help: Ask someone to look, or check for a red glow reflected in a window, wall or garage door behind the car.

opts.a: I'm not sure / I can't check

q_electronic.q: Does the car start and run normally, with bright dash lights?

opts.a: No, it won't start, or the lights are dim
Yes, but it still won't leave Park, or there's a shifter warning message

result.title: The car's weight is pressing on the Park lock
result.now: Set the parking brake, start the engine, press the brake pedal firmly, and shift out of Park with a firm, steady pull rather than a jerk.
if: If it releases with a clunk, that's normal in this situation. Next time, set the parking brake before you shift into Park on a slope.
If it still won't move, check whether the brake lights work. The problem may be electrical instead.
result.why: When you park on a slope and shift into Park before setting the parking brake, the car rolls slightly until its weight rests on a small metal pin in the transmission (the Park pawl). That load can make the shifter very hard to move. It's not a fault, but it puts extra stress on parts if it happens often.

causes.name: Car's weight on the Park pawl
causes.clues: Parked on a slope, and the shifter feels jammed rather than locked.
causes.against: If the car is on flat ground, look at the brake lights and battery instead.

causes.name: Shift lock not releasing
causes.clues: The brake lights don't work, or you don't hear a faint click near the shifter when you press the brake.

causes.name: Binding shift cable
causes.clues: The shifter has felt stiff in every position lately.

you: Set the parking brake before shifting into Park on any slope.
Check whether the brake lights work.
shop: Park pawl inspection if it keeps happening

result.title: A faulty brake light switch or a blown fuse is the likely cause
result.now: Check the fuse for the brake lights or stop lamps (your owner's manual shows which one) and replace it if it's blown.
if: If the fuse is fine, the brake light switch near the top of the brake pedal is likely bad. Have it replaced within a few days, and avoid driving until the brake lights work, especially in traffic or after dark.
If a new fuse blows right away, there's a short in the wiring that a shop needs to find.
If you must move the car before then, use the shift lock release, a small slot or button near the shifter (see your owner's manual).
result.why: The car only unlocks the shifter when it gets a signal that the brake is pressed, and on most cars that signal comes from the brake light switch. No brake lights plus a locked shifter almost always means the switch or its fuse. It's a common and usually simple fix, but brake lights are essential so drivers behind you know you're stopping.

causes.name: Failed brake light switch
causes.clues: The brake lights stopped working, and on many cars the cruise control won't engage either.

causes.name: Blown stop lamp fuse
causes.clues: All the brake lights went out at once, including the center one.

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem
causes.clues: The brake lights flicker or work some of the time.

you: Note whether the cruise control still works.

result.title: The shift lock itself is likely sticking or has failed
result.now: Use the shift lock release: with the parking brake set and your foot on the brake, press into the small slot or button near the shifter (your owner's manual shows where) while you move the shifter out of Park.
if: If the release lets you shift, get the shift lock checked when convenient so you don't get stuck again somewhere inconvenient.
If even the release doesn't free it, the shift cable or the shifter itself may be damaged. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
result.why: Working brake lights mean the brake signal is probably fine. The problem is more likely the small electric lock (solenoid) in the shifter that's supposed to release, or something jamming the shifter, like a spilled drink that has gone sticky. The manual release bypasses that lock.

causes.name: Failed shift lock solenoid
causes.clues: You don't hear a faint click from the shifter when you press the brake.

causes.name: Sticky residue or debris in the shifter
causes.clues: A drink was spilled near the console, or it's worse in hot weather.

causes.name: Worn or misadjusted brake switch
causes.clues: It sometimes works if you press the brake harder.

you: With the cabin quiet, listen for a faint click near the shifter when you press the brake.

result.title: A weak or dead battery is keeping the shifter locked
result.now: Jump-start the car or use a battery booster, then press the brake firmly and try the shifter again.
if: If it shifts once the car has power, have the battery and charging system tested soon.
If you need to move the car without power, your owner's manual explains the shift lock release, or how to put an electronic shifter in Neutral for towing.
result.why: The shift lock, and electronic shifters in particular, need electrical power to release. With a dead or weak battery they stay locked even though nothing is wrong with the transmission.

causes.name: Dead or weak battery
causes.clues: Dim dash lights, slow cranking, or the car sat for a while.

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery cable
causes.clues: Crusty buildup on the terminals, or a cable you can wiggle.

causes.name: Charging system problem
causes.clues: The battery light came on while driving recently.

you: Try a jump start or a booster pack.

result.title: The shift cable has likely broken or come loose
result.now: Set the parking brake firmly and don't drive it. Have it towed or have a mobile mechanic come to you.
if: If you're not certain which gear the transmission is actually in, block the wheels too before you get out.
If the shifter feels loose or floppy, a broken cable bushing is very likely, which is usually a small repair.
result.why: The shifter is connected to the transmission by a cable. When the cable or the small bushing that holds it breaks, the shifter moves but the transmission stays where it was. The car can't be shifted reliably, and you can't trust Park to hold it.

causes.name: Broken shift cable bushing
causes.clues: The shifter feels loose or floppy.

causes.name: Stretched, broken or disconnected shift cable
causes.clues: The shifter moves through the positions with almost no resistance.

causes.name: Fault in the transmission's shift mechanism
causes.clues: The cable checks out fine.
causes.against: Much less common than a cable or bushing problem.

you: Note whether the dash gear display changes when you move the shifter.

result.title: The electronic shifter or one of its sensors may have a fault
result.now: Turn the car off, wait a minute, then restart it with your foot firmly on the brake and try again. If it still won't leave Park, contact a dealer or repair shop.
if: If a transmission or shifter warning stays on, have it towed rather than forcing it. Your owner's manual explains how to put the car in Neutral for towing.
Check for open recalls on your car by VIN on the NHTSA recalls site. Some electronic shifters have been recalled.
result.why: Push-button and dial shifters don't move the transmission directly. They send a signal to a control module, which needs good battery voltage, a brake signal and working sensors. If any of those is missing, the car may keep itself in Park as a safety measure.

causes.name: Low battery voltage
causes.clues: Slow cranking, or other electrical glitches.

causes.name: Brake signal not detected
causes.clues: The brake lights don't work.

causes.name: Shifter, sensor or control module fault
causes.clues: A warning message on the dash.

you: Restart the car with your foot firmly on the brake.
Check that the brake lights work.
shop: Code scan of the transmission and shifter modules

result.title: Start with the common, simple causes
result.now: With the parking brake set, turn the key to ON or start the engine, press the brake firmly and try again. If it won't move, use the shift lock release near the shifter (your owner's manual shows where).
if: If the dash is dim or the car won't start, the battery is the likely cause.
If the release works, find out why within a few days, starting with whether the brake lights work.
result.why: Most cars stuck in Park have one of a few simple problems: the brake signal isn't reaching the shift lock, the battery is weak, or the car's weight is resting on the Park lock. The shift lock release lets you move the car while you sort out which.

causes.name: Brake light switch or fuse
causes.clues: The brake lights don't work.

causes.name: Weak battery
causes.clues: Dim dash lights or slow cranking.

causes.name: Car parked on a slope
causes.clues: The shifter feels jammed rather than locked.

you: Have someone check the brake lights.
